text:
pagerbot: 🚨 INCIDENT AUTO-PAGE: Unusual auth traffic + signed-cookie beaconing detected against /v1/auth/login from multiple IP clusters. Priority: P1. On-call: @sre-oncall. Pager details: https://pager.example/INC-2150008888

sre-oncall: Got it. I'm looking. Which services affected?

michelle: Seeing 502s and auth latencies in edge-proxy logs, plus repeated signed cookie reuse across tenants. Small sample: 
```
edge-proxy: 2026-03-18T14:21:10Z src=34.89.12.5 method=POST path=/v1/auth/login status=200 cookie=signed_v2=eyJhb... reused_for_tenant=acme-corp
edge-proxy: 2026-03-18T14:21:11Z src=52.19.22.11 method=GET path=/internal/kv status=403 cookie=signed_v2=eyJhb...
```

tobias: Are we sure those cookie values are valid tokens or just replayed copies?

michelle: Looks like replayed signed cookies (same signature) hitting different tenant scopes. Could be exfil -> replay.

sec-eng: Copy. Pulling auth service logs and token issuance traces. Initial hypothesis: a leak from a misconfigured staging forwarder that included Set-Cookie headers.

infra-eng: Confirmed an S3 forwarder job in staging pushed archived logs with full headers to a public bucket for 12h earlier today. Investigating ACLs now.

sre-oncall: Action list (short): 1) Quarantine abused cookie families (denylist at edge). 2) Rotate any affected service signing keys if exposed. 3) Confirm S3 ACLs and remove public objects. 4) Customer-impact assessment & comms. Assigning tasks.

michelle: Doing denylist rule now at edge WAF to drop requests with header Cookie matching signature prefix `eyJhb`. Pushing rule: `wafctl rules add deny-cookie-replay --match "Cookie: signed_v2=eyJhb" --action block`

infra-eng: Found objects: s3://staging-logs/public-archive/2026-03-18/edge-headers-*.gz (public-read). Taking them private and starting download for root cause. Command: `aws s3 cp s3://staging-logs/public-archive/2026-03-18/edge-headers-001.gz /tmp/`

sec-eng: While infra locks bucket, we'll treat signing key KMS alias arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:alias/auth-signing-prod as potentially impacted until proven otherwise. Starting emergency rotation plan.

sre-oncall: Michelle, confirm WAF rule active and give me hit counts. Tobias, pls prepare rollback plan for the denylist if false positive observed. sec-eng, estimate time for KMS key rotation and key import for new signing key.

michelle: WAF rule active. Hits: 1,240 blocked in first 5m. Most from 34.89.0.0/16 and 52.19.0.0/16 clusters.

tobias: Rollback plan: remove rule `wafctl rules delete deny-cookie-replay` and allowlist any false-positive IPs. Will monitor 10m window before full removal.

sec-eng: KMS rotation: generate new signing key in KMS, test-sign on staging, then update auth service key id. Estimated 30-45m for staged rollout and verification. Will also queue emergency rotate of any short-lived tokens we can invalidate.

customer-success: Any immediate customer-facing impact? Do we need to open a support bridge?

sre-oncall: So far no confirmed session hijacking reports. We should prepare an advisory if exfil confirmed. Customer-impact: incomplete but potential replayable cookies could allow access to tenant-scoped endpoints until tokens expire or we rotate keys. Recommend CS draft a hold-notification template. @legal loop in if we suspect data exposure.

legal: On it. If the S3 objects contained identifiable PII, we may have disclosure obligations. Keep a manifest of affected tenants and timeline.

michelle: Quick sanity check: we added short-term mitigation (denylist). Auth service still healthy. CPU spiked 10% but within SLO.

infra-eng: ACLs fixed. Objects made private and lifecycle paused. Downloading archived files for forensics. MD5sums saved to evidence bucket `s3://sec-evidence/INC-2150008888/`.

sec-eng: Forensics: sample headers show Set-Cookie lines including `HttpOnly` but not `SameSite=Strict`. That could allow cross-site replay from an exfiltrate. Also saw staging pipeline which gzipped and uploaded raw HTTP logs without masking.

sre-oncall: Next steps: 1) Maintain denylist and monitoring. 2) Rotate signing key (sec-eng). 3) Reissue short TTL session tokens where possible (auth service flag rotate-now). 4) Provide customers a timeline and mitigation guidance (CS + legal). 5) Post-mortem and runbook update (ops). Assigning owners in thread.

sec-eng: Starting KMS key creation and will post the new key id in ~35m. Plan to sign with new key and invalidate old signatures by bumping key id in token verifier.

tobias: I can add a temporary token-blacklist endpoint to auth service to revoke currently active tokens issued in last 24h if required. Deploying patch to staging for fast enable.

customer-success: Drafting notice: short summary, what we did, recommended customer actions: rotate integration tokens, rotate service credentials, verify sessions. Will keep it non-alarming.

legal: Preparing internal timeline and retention hold. Need list of affected tenants. Sec-eng / infra please populate `affected_tenants.txt` in evidence bucket.

michelle: Adding short script we ran to detect duplicates: 
```bash
zcat edge-headers-*.gz | jq -r '.headers.Set-Cookie' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 50
```

sec-eng: Uploaded `affected_tenants.txt` with 6 tenant ids to s3://sec-evidence/INC-2150008888/affected_tenants.txt.

sre-oncall: Customer-impact status: Potential sensitive cookies in public bucket for ~12h. No confirmed session takeover. CS to prepare outreach if rotation confirms keys exposed.

pagerbot: Incident status updated: mitigation in progress. Post-mortem channel will be created after containment: #postmortems-INC-2150008888

michelle: Quick note — monitoring shows a secondary spike from a new IP block after the denylist; adding rate-limit rule and notifying upstream provider for possible abuse.

tobias: Patch to add token-blacklist endpoint merged and will be hotpatched to prod in 20m.

sec-eng: New KMS key created: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345. Starting rollout to verifier and signer.

sre-oncall: Good work. Keep updates here. If anyone sees customer escalations, ping @customer-success immediately and cc legal. We'll keep this page open until rotation and reissue complete.

legal: Noted. We'll wait for final affected_tenants list before deciding external disclosure timing.

customer-success: I'll stand by for the final customer list and PR template.

michelle: WAF + rate-limit + edge denylist holding. Blocked ~4k requests in last 30m. No false positives so far.

sec-eng: Rotation complete, verifier and signer switched to new key id. Old key disabled in KMS (not deleted) for safeguards. Next: reissue sessions and monitor anomalies for 24h.

sre-oncall: Closing loop: containment achieved, rotation done, CS & legal on comms. Creating follow-up postmortem task and runbook updates. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
